 Police investigate attempted stabbing on UIC campus, building evacuated 
 "Authorities are responding. Avoid the area until further notice," the UIC alert stated. 
 By Alex Dvorak • 
 Published November 4, 2026 • 
 Updated 4 hours ago 
 BOOKMARKER 
 NBC Universal, Inc. 
 “Authorities are responding. Avoid the area until further notice,” the UIC alert stated.
 People were being told to avoid part of the University of Illinois Chicago campus Wednesday afternoon as police activity was reported in a student center building. 
 An alert from the school said police activity was reported around 12:40 p.m. at 750 S. Halsted St. on the second floor of the building, which is the Student Center East Tower.

   WATCH HERE 
 "Authorities are responding. Avoid the area until further notice," the alert stated.
 Around 1:30 p.m., the school said it was evacuating the building. 
 "If you are not on campus, avoid the area until further notice," a separate alert stated. 
 In a statement to NBC Chicago, the university said police were investigating "an attempted stabbing" on the second floor of the Student Center East. 
 The incident involved two UIC students, one of whom was arrested and taken into custody.

 The school said the other student "was neither stabbed nor injured." 
 "The area has been secured, and there is no threat to the campus community. Student Center East was evacuated as a precaution and remains closed while the investigation continues," the statement read. 
 Multiple witnesses reported the suspect chased students and nearly slashed one with a large kitchen knife.
 Chicago police confirmed they were at the scene assisting university police with the response. 
 Later Wednesday afternoon, UIC said the Student Center East would remain closed for the remainder of the day. FBI and ATF agents could be seen entering the building, though details on why were not released.
